name: cal11059

original_issue.reason: After successfully refreshing and persisting `accessTokenParsed.data`, the connection is still initialized from `credentialKey`, the pre-refresh credential. In the normal expired-token case that caused the refresh, subsequent Salesforce operations therefore authenticate with the expired access token; it also ignores the refreshed `instance_url`. The successful refresh does not make the current service instance usable.
original_issue.suggestedFixDescription: Construct the connection with `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url`; retain the existing refresh token because Salesforce does not rotate it here.
original_issue.suggestedFixDiff:
--- a/packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts
+++ b/packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts
@@ -101,8 +101,8 @@ export default class SalesforceCalendarService implements Calendar {
       clientId: consumer_key,
       clientSecret: consumer_secret,
       redirectUri: WEBAPP_URL + "/api/integrations/salesforce/callback",
-      instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url,
-      accessToken: credentialKey.access_token,
+      instanceUrl: accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url,
+      accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token,
       refreshToken: credentialKey.refresh_token,
original_issue.title: Connection discards refreshed access token

name: firefox4

original_issue.reason: After `checkCopiedUrl()` was removed from `testClipboard`, every operation that pastes and validates the copied URL is inside this iOS 17 availability block. On iOS 16 and earlier the test copies the URL, creates a tab, opens the URL bar, and then exits without an assertion or any other check of the clipboard result, so a broken copy operation passes silently.
original_issue.suggestedFixDescription: Restore a pre-iOS 17 clipboard assertion (for example, call the existing `checkCopiedUrl()` on the OS versions it supports), or explicitly skip unsupported versions rather than reporting a passing test with no verification.
original_issue.title: Pre-iOS 17 test has no verification
